analysis.title: US TMT 5 x 5 - 1 Nov 2026 (Peter Callahan)
key_insights: The NDX is in its third 10%+ drawdown (correction) of 2026. It fell about 7% in October, its second worst month since the AI cycle began in early 2023.

The AI demand engine (token demand and GW/DC build-outs) is described as intact. Risk appetite has fallen sharply, with GS' Global Risk Appetite Indicator posting one of its largest monthly drops in 5+ years, as the market questions how linear the AI build-out is beyond CY27. This is pressuring multiples across the board.
The Mon-Wed bounce was faded. A benign FOMC meeting and robust 3Q earnings did not restart momentum in Tech/AI.

Investors want to broaden out of AI, but the author calls this hard. Non-AI leadership days feel like unwinds, and few non-semis/AI names are free of AI disruption narratives. The author does not sense a bearish directional tilt on AI suppliers.

Several names fell sharply on the day after earnings, some to their worst days ever: NOW -25%, INTC -30%, RDDT -30%, SNDK -13%, Eoptolink -15%, FFIV -20%, CAT -9%, Adyen -13%. The prior week's moves included TTMI -27% and LRCX -12%. The author links this to crowded positioning, a truncated calendar and ongoing secular debates.
Names that pulled back or lagged out of earnings and have an idiosyncratic angle or are out of consensus, to revisit: TWLO, SNDK, RBLX, MSFT, AMZN, NOW, APH, Adyen, NXPI.

Semis closed down about 7% on Friday. The SOX closed below its 200-dma after 355 consecutive sessions above it, the 3rd longest streak in 10 years, and is retesting the July low. Its forward P/E is back at AI-cycle lows, around 16x.

Semis earnings debate points: Kioxia guided 4Q bit shipments flat q/q on timing of longer-lead-time products, though CY27 capacity is effectively sold out. MSFT capex came in under budget in 3Q on third-party capacity delays, though it guided to a 2H FY capex acceleration. INTC guided PC revenue down about 20% q/q in 4Q and expects the inventory correction to extend into 1H27, while seeing server CPU demand accelerating on agentic AI. Eoptolink cited flooding delays, VMI adoption uncertainty and DSP supply tightness. AMKR and Vanchip gave weak smartphone read-outs.
The author calls these datapoints rate-of-change signals that sit away from the AI complex. AMZN guiding to 2 years of forward AWS revenue visibility is cited as evidence of AI strength.

Top client questions: what happened Friday, new Mag 7 preferences, why MSFT faded, whether investors are cutting out-year estimates or only Semis multiples, the path for NOW after its print, whether the FTNT-driven Security drawdown is defended, earnings set-ups (AAPL, DDOG, OTAs, NET, AMD), and whether E-commerce is inflecting (EBAY and ETSY citing AI growth tailwinds).

AAPL enters Monday's earnings at an all-time high multiple, 36x forward P/E and a 17x premium to the S&P 500. Focus areas are 3Q Services growth, gross margin and guidance (cost inflation, pricing, services mix), and the 4Q revenue guide. GIR expects total revenue growth guidance of low-to-mid single digits y/y.

UBER has sold off the day after earnings in 8 of its last 10 prints despite steady beats. It enters at about 10x EV/EBITDA and a P/E/G below 0.5x, and the author asks whether this print breaks the trend.
NET has had about 5 straight quarters of accelerating or stable revenue growth. Bulls want that to continue into 2027+ on agentic activity (Workers, Pay per crawl).

MCHP: analog semis have de-rated over recent months despite ISM near cycle highs. The question is whether MCHP, after solid results from TXN and NXPI, can position the group as a core holding into 2027.
TTWO is called one of the most idiosyncratic names in TMT. The question is whether it can find support ahead of a GTA 6 fueled year-end rally.

Week ahead catalysts: US Midterm Election on Tue 11/3 (GIR expects the focus on data centers to fade after it), BoE decision Thu 11/5, US NFPs Fri 11/6, and heavy tech earnings (AAPL, PLTR, AMD, ANET, QCOM, ARM, UBER, DDOG, NET, MCHP, ABNB, LYV).
